verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean map is `x ↦ referencePair O d S + (1/(2Λ)) • naturalRemainder O d S (1/Λ) a x`, with S = naturalResolvent = (1+T)^{-1} when it is instantiated in `natural_axis_profiles`. Centre: S d.one is Φ⁰ = (1+T)^{-1}1, and -(1/2)·𝒥₁(L⁻¹Z*) is 𝔲⁰ = -YZ*/(2L), since 𝒥₁ of a radially constant c is cY by (B.5) with ν = 1. Increments: the Λ⁻¹ prefactor 1/(2Λ) and the two components match (1+T)^{-1}𝒥₂R₁/(2Λ) and 𝒥₁R₂/(2Λ) term by term with LR₁, LR₂ of p.147, with three packaging differences: the radial inverses are applied to each monomial of LR₁, LR₂ separately, the terms carrying a logarithmic radial or parameter derivative using the composites dot1/dot2, param1/param2, mixed1/mixed2 (the bound (B.6) of Lemma B.1); multiplication by L⁻¹ is performed outside the radial inverses rather than inside R₁, R₂, which agrees because L⁻¹ has radial degree zero (recorded in the AxisData docstring, AxisContraction.lean:302, but not required by the statement); and the Λ⁻¹ parts of W = W_* + Λ⁻¹B and H_c = H_* + Λ⁻¹d𝔲 are carried as a separate t·slow term with t = 1/Λ, the regrouping being checked as the ring identities `angular_remainder_expansion` (line 373) and `axial_remainder_expansion` (line 386). `fixedPoint_integrated_equations` (line 618) converts the fixed-point equation back into the two integrated equations, so the use of the map is the paper's.
